categories.main_business_segments: Nexstar Media Group operates primarily in one reportable broadcast segment, which includes its portfolio of local television stations, national cable news network NewsNation, multicast networks (Antenna TV and REWIND TV), and a radio station. Other activities include The CW Network (in which Nexstar holds a majority stake), digital businesses focused on national markets (such as The Hill and BestReviews), and corporate/real estate management functions. The company also holds a significant equity interest in TV Food Network.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Nexstar's core operations rely on broadcast television technology, including the adoption of the ATSC 3.0 (NextGen TV) standard for high-speed data transmission and enhanced broadcast capabilities. The company produces over 316,000 hours of local and national news, sports, and entertainment content annually, leveraging a large network of journalists and production staff. Digital content is distributed via proprietary websites, mobile apps, OTT applications, and FAST channels, with monetization through both direct and programmatic advertising sales.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Nexstar serves a diverse customer base including local, regional, and national advertisers, multichannel video programming distributors (MVPDs), virtual MVPDs (vMVPDs), and digital advertisers. Key end markets include local and national television audiences, political advertisers (especially in election years), and digital consumers seeking news, entertainment, and product reviews. No single customer accounts for more than 13% of revenue, and the company has relationships with over 40,000 advertisers.
categories.geographic_coverage: Nexstar operates in 116 U.S. markets across 40 states and the District of Columbia, reaching approximately 70% of U.S. television households through its owned and partner stations. Its national networks, including The CW and NewsNation, provide coast-to-coast coverage, while digital assets attract nearly 103 million monthly unique users nationwide. The company’s reach includes major DMAs such as New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago.
categories.supply_chain_position: Nexstar operates at the downstream end of the media supply chain, focusing on content production, aggregation, and direct distribution to consumers via broadcast, cable, and digital platforms. The company also acts as a content licensor to MVPDs/vMVPDs and provides spectrum for third-party programmers on multicast channels.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Nexstar’s strategic priorities include leveraging its scale to grow distribution and advertising revenues, expanding and improving national network assets (notably The CW and NewsNation), and developing new revenue streams through ATSC 3.0-enabled data services. The company is focused on cost discipline, operational efficiency, and selective acquisitions to enhance its platform. Innovation themes include unbiased news, sports programming expansion, and digital product development.
categories.revenue_model: The company generates revenue primarily through contractual distribution fees from MVPDs and vMVPDs (54% of 2024 revenue), advertising sales (45%, including local, national, political, and digital advertising), and other sources such as spectrum leasing and affiliate fees. Digital revenues are derived from display/video advertising and affiliate commissions (e.g., BestReviews). Revenue is diversified by geography, customer, and network affiliation.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Nexstar competes with other broadcast station groups (e.g., Gray Television, TEGNA, Sinclair, Scripps), national broadcast and cable networks (e.g., Fox, Paramount, Warner Bros. Discovery), and digital media platforms (e.g., Google, Meta, YouTube, streaming services). It is the largest local television broadcaster in the U.S. and the largest affiliate group for each major broadcast network, with strong national brands and a top 10 digital news property.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, Nexstar generated record net revenue of $5.4 billion, up 9.6% from 2023, with net income attributable to Nexstar of $722 million. The company returned $820 million to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases, and maintained a high leverage profile with $6.5 billion in debt (74.3% of capitalization). Growth is driven by political advertising cycles, distribution fee escalations, and digital expansion, with a history of both organic and acquisition-led growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Nexstar emphasizes its unique combination of scaled local audiences and national reach, offering advertisers and distributors access to both granular local markets and broad national platforms. Its focus on politically neutral, reliable news, strong local franchises, and diversified revenue streams differentiates it from peers. The company’s operational efficiency, innovation in ATSC 3.0, and ability to monetize both traditional and digital platforms underpin its competitive advantage.
